results.title: Policy preferences in response to large forced migration inflows - ScienceDirect
results.content: We examine the multidimensional character of migration policy preferences, and whether humanitarian values matter for these preferences. We conducted a pre-registered conjoint experiment in Colombia in 2021 (N = 2,508), a major host of forced migrants globally. Colombians favor fewer restrictions on Venezuelans’ right to work, healthcare access, family reunification, or location within Colombia. There is support for placing some restrictions on the number of Venezuelans entering the country and the length of their residence in Colombia. Respondents holding stronger humanitarian preferences favor fewer restrictions in domains addressing core needs of health, family, and work. In response, we conducted a pre-registered conjoint experiment (N = 2,508) fielded in Colombia, the country that has received the largest share of Venezuelan emigrants who themselves currently comprise one of the world’s largest migratory flows. However, there is support for restrictions on the overall number of Venezuelans allowed to settle in the country, as well as the length of time that Venezuelans are allowed to stay in Colombia.
